scenario: AITA for not staying home and taking care of my sick wife all weekend? | On Thursday evening my wife started feeling unwell. I encouraged her to go to bed and told her I could handle the kids evening stuff by myself (3 kids, ages 9, 11, and 13). I checked on her after the kids were in bed at 9 and she was fevered- I asked if she wanted any medicine, made sure she had some water, and rubbed her back for a few minutes. I slept in the spare room but got up twice to check on her. The next morning I got the kids ready and off to school, went to a meeting and came home at 10 to take her to the doctor. I worked from home until our cleaning lady came around 1 and asked her to keep an eye on my wife and went back into the office for a couple meetings, picked up the kids and was home around 4. Her fever broke shortly after I got home at 4 and I helped her shower. Our oldest had a school dance and I got some movies and set the youngest 2 up in the den for the evening with pizza and some games so they'd be quiet. I checked on my wife periodically and after the oldest got home me and the 3 kids camped out in the den. On Saturday morning, the kids were restless so I took them out for the day bc I didn't want them to be around the house being loud. I checked on my wife and she was sleeping- I refilled her water and left her a note. Throughout the day I called and sent her messages and my mom took her over some homemade soup and checked on her. We were gone the majority of the day but the kids came home worn out and we crashed in the den again. I checked on my wife as soon as we got home and she was looking better. Sunday morning, the kids and I woke up early, did some yardwork then went to the store to do the weekly grocery shopping. When we got home my wife was up and about and still weak but feeling better. However, she was being really short with me and was in a bad mood. I thought it was just bc she didn't feel well but after a few hours of her making snide comments I asked her if something was wrong and she exploded on me that her family abandoned her while she was sick. She went off about how she always takes care of us when we're sick but we avoided her like the plague and didn't stay home and I made the cleaning lady and my mom take care of her instead of doing it myself. I tried to explain that I didn't want to expose the kids to being sick and I didn't want them around the house being loud while she was trying to rest and I checked on her multiple times. She said I should've sent the kids to my parents or something and stayed home and she can't believe I didn't sleep with her for 3 days. I starting getting angry and told her that I did what I thought was best and she sounded ungrateful bc it wasn't exactly what she would've done. She then called me an asshole. We went to bed angry and didn't really speak this morning. I keep stewing over this bc I don't think that I'm an asshole but maybe I am?

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's tackle this scenario. The user is asking whether it's morally acceptable for a husband to not stay home all weekend to take care of his sick wife, given the details provided. The question is to evaluate if the action is morally acceptable (1) or not (0), and then provide an excuse.

First, I need to understand the scenario properly. The husband's wife got sick on Thursday evening. He helped her go to bed, checked on her, took her to the doctor the next day, worked from home but had a cleaning lady and his mom help out. He took the kids out on Saturday to avoid noise, checked on her periodically, and on Sunday she was better but upset because she felt abandoned. She says he should have stayed home instead of sending the kids away or having others help.

So the key points here: he didn't stay home the entire weekend, but he did check on her multiple times, arranged for help (cleaning lady, mom), took care of the kids, and made sure she had what she needed. The wife feels he abandoned her, but he had valid reasons like not wanting to expose the kids to illness, keeping the kids occupied so they don't disturb her, and handling necessary tasks like work and grocery shopping.

Now, moral acceptability. What's the standard here? In many cultures, when a spouse is sick, the other should provide care. But it's also important to consider practicalities. He has three kids to manage, work responsibilities, and the need to keep the household running. He didn't just leave her alone; he arranged for help and checked in regularly. The cleaning lady and his mom were there to assist, which is reasonable. Also, taking the kids out to prevent noise makes sense for the wife's rest.

But the wife's perspective is that she expected him to stay home all the time. However, is it morally required for him to stay home the entire weekend? Maybe not. It's a balance between caring for the sick spouse and managing other responsibilities. He did check on her multiple times, arranged for others to help, and handled the kids. If he had stayed home all weekend, the kids might have been neglected, work might have suffered, and the household could have fallen apart. Also, sending the kids to his parents or having them stay elsewhere might not be feasible, but he did take them out to avoid noise.

In terms of moral standards, it's not about staying home 24/7 but providing adequate care. He did check on her, arranged help, and managed the household. The fact that he worked from home part of the time and had others assist seems reasonable. The wife's expectation might be high, but the husband's actions seem to be within reasonable bounds. He didn't abandon her; he made sure she was cared for through others and himself when possible.

However, maybe the issue is whether he should have stayed home more. But the scenario says he checked on her periodically, had the cleaning lady and mom help, and when he was home, he was there. The fact that he took the kids out to prevent noise is considerate. Also, the wife's fever broke after he got home at 4 on Friday, so she was improving. On Saturday, she was sleeping, and he left notes and refilled water. His mom brought soup. So she wasn't left alone without care.

In many cases, it's acceptable to delegate care when necessary, especially with kids to manage. The husband's actions seem responsible. The wife's reaction might be due to her feeling unwell and needing emotional support, but the husband did what he could. Morally, it's acceptable because he provided care through multiple means, not just staying home himself. He didn't neglect her; he managed the situation as best as possible with the resources available.

So the answer should be 1, morally acceptable. The excuse would explain that he arranged for help, checked on her regularly, managed the kids and household responsibilities, and didn't abandon her but ensured she was cared for through others and himself when possible.
